metadata.title: Micron faces Taiwan uncertainty as labor dispute threatens expansion, report warns

content.text:
Investing.com -- Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) expansion plans in Taiwan could face further uncertainty as an escalating labor dispute raises the prospect of the U.S. memory chipmaker redirecting future investments to Singapore, Taiwan's Commercial Times reported on Thursday, citing Wealth Magazine chairman Hsieh Chin-ho.
Hsieh warned that deteriorating labor relations could prompt Micron's board to reconsider investments in Taiwan worth a combined NT$1.6 trillion. In a worst-case scenario, the company could close its Taoyuan facility and lay off around 3,000 employees, he said.
The dispute centres on demands by workers for a more transparent profit-sharing arrangement as Micron benefits from surging demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence infrastructure. The Taoyuan union has sought to have 15% of the company's operating profit distributed to employees, arguing that existing bonus arrangements do not adequately reflect its financial performance.
Micron and its larger Taichung union reached a labor agreement in October, but the separate dispute in Taoyuan has remained unresolved. The Taoyuan union subsequently withdrew from further negotiations in November after failing to secure the profit-sharing arrangement, according to earlier reports.
Hsieh said Micron could instead direct new investments towards Singapore, where it stands to benefit from more attractive investment incentives. He also warned that continued labor instability could jeopardise plans to upgrade the Taoyuan facility, including the potential installation of more than 10 advanced extreme ultraviolet lithography machines.
Micron had previously suspended plans for a new Taoyuan manufacturing facility, Bloomberg reported in November, amid concerns over the labor dispute. The proposed project was estimated to involve investments of $3 billion to $4.5 billion.
Micron said at the time that its Taiwan operations were continuing normally and that it remained confident in maintaining stable operations without disrupting customer supply. The company also said it would continue seeking a constructive resolution with the Taoyuan union.
